claims.claim: Japan has no wealth tax

sources.name: PwC: Japan, other taxes
sources.says: Last reviewed 07 August 2026. "There are currently no net wealth/worth taxes in Japan." Inheritance tax is levied on recipients; "The basic exemption is JPY 30 million plus JPY 6 million per statutory heir"; rates 10% to 55%, 55% on a taxable amount over JPY 600,000,000. Transfers of overseas assets from foreign nationals with a 'Jusho' in Japan for less than ten of the last 15 years who hold a Table 1 visa are exempt; Table 1 "does not include ... permanent resident, spouse or child of a Japanese national". The page does not cover an exit tax.

sources.name: PwC: quick chart, net wealth/worth tax rates
sources.says: Australia (30 June 2026), Japan (07 August 2026), New Zealand (06 July 2026), Singapore (02 July 2026), Taiwan (20 August 2026) and the Republic of Korea (04 June 2026) are all "NA": "the territory does not have the indicated tax".

claims.claim: A foreign resident is a non-permanent resident for the first 5 of 10 years, taxed on foreign dividends and interest only when paid in or remitted to Japan

sources.name: PwC: Japan, residence
sources.says: Last reviewed 07 August 2026. "A resident taxpayer who is not a Japanese national and whose aggregate stay in Japan is five years or less within the preceding ten years is classified as a non-permanent resident taxpayer."

sources.name: PwC: Japan, taxes on personal income
sources.says: Last reviewed 07 August 2026. "Non-permanent resident taxpayers are taxed on Japan-sourced income and foreign-source income only to the extent that it is paid in Japan or remitted to Japan." National income tax tops out at 45% over JPY 40 million; a 2.1% surtax on national tax applies; local inhabitant's tax "at a flat rate of 10%".

claims.note: "how borrowed money sent in is treated needs advice" is a hedge, not a claim; nothing read addresses it.

claims.claim: A non-permanent resident is taxed on gains from securities bought while living in Japan (since April 2017) whether or not remitted; holdings bought before arrival stay on the remittance basis

sources.name: National Tax Agency: Income Tax Basic Circular, chapter 2 (scope of taxable income), 7-1
sources.says: Undated (page text partly garbled in Shift_JIS). Circular 7-1 defines 特定有価証券 as securities acquired more than 10 years before, acquired during the 10 years while the person was not a non-permanent resident, or acquired on or before 31 March 2017.

sources.name: Deloitte (Legal 500): change in taxation of non-permanent residents
sources.says: Dated 20 January 2017. "Effective from 1 April 2017" an NPR's gains on shares or securities can be excluded "with the exception of those relating to shares or securities acquired by a non-permanent resident after 1 April 2017"; taxation is limited to "acquisitions subsequent to the later of 1 April 2017 or their arrival in Japan."

claims.note: The NTA circular defines the protected securities (bought over 10 years ago, bought while not a non-permanent resident, or bought by 31 March 2017); Legal 500 (Deloitte, 2017) explains the April 2017 change. The 2017 page is older than the source order prefers; the circular is the primary text, though WebFetch returned it partly garbled.

claims.claim: After 5 years, worldwide income: 20.315% on listed-share dividends and capital gains, US-listed included

sources.name: PwC: Japan, income determination
sources.says: Last reviewed 07 August 2026. Listed-company dividends "can optionally be taxed separately ... at a flat rate of 20.315%"; gains on certain securities including shares are "taxed separately ... at a flat rate of 20.315%"; "Listed shares" means "shares listed on Japanese or foreign stock exchanges"; "Interest paid by offshore financial institutions is taxed at graduated rates."

sources.name: National Tax Agency: Tax Answer No.1463, listed shares (上場株式等)
sources.says: As of 1 April 2026 (令和8年4月1日現在法令等). 上場株式等 include "外国金融商品市場において売買されている株式等" (shares traded on a foreign market); gains are taxed at 15% national plus 5% local, with the 2.1% reconstruction surtax on the national tax.

sources.name: National Tax Agency: Tax Answer No.1330, dividends
sources.says: As of 1 April 2026. Listed-share dividends are withheld at 15.315% (plus 5% local) and may be taxed by comprehensive taxation, separate self-assessment (申告分離課税) or left out of the return.

claims.claim: Leaving after more than 5 of 10 years of residence outside Table I statuses with JPY 100m or more in securities triggers an exit tax on unrealised gains

sources.name: National Tax Agency: Tax Answer No.1478, exit tax
sources.says: As of 1 April 2026. Subject to the exit tax: residents whose covered assets total "1億円以上" at departure and who, "原則として", had a domicile or residence in Japan for more than 5 of the 10 years before departure. The page does not mention residence statuses.

sources.name: Toma Consultants: basics of Japan's exit tax
sources.says: Dated 2025/05/15. Conditions: "Own over 100 million yen in subjected assets, both in Japan and overseas" and a domicile or residence in Japan "for over 5 of the last 10 years", "Excluding period of stay under a status listed in Table I of the Immigration Control and Refugee Recognition Act."

claims.note: The NTA page gives the JPY 100m and 5-of-10-years tests "as a rule"; the Table I exclusion is from Toma (2025). No change was found in the FY2027 tax reform requests (searched November 2026). localTaxes.ts does not model the exit tax.
claims.modelMismatch: localTaxes.ts (JP) models only inheritance tax; the exit tax on unrealised gains (securities of JPY 100m+, after 5 of 10 years outside Table I statuses) is not modelled. A Long Stay visitor never reaches it.

claims.claim: A foreign national on a Table I status such as Long Stay is taxed only on Japan-sited assets until 10 of the last 15 years in Japan; statuses outside Table I (spouse of a Japanese national, permanent resident) put the worldwide estate in reach from the start

sources.name: PwC: Japan, other taxes
sources.says: Last reviewed 07 August 2026. "There are currently no net wealth/worth taxes in Japan." Inheritance tax is levied on recipients; "The basic exemption is JPY 30 million plus JPY 6 million per statutory heir"; rates 10% to 55%, 55% on a taxable amount over JPY 600,000,000. Transfers of overseas assets from foreign nationals with a 'Jusho' in Japan for less than ten of the last 15 years who hold a Table 1 visa are exempt; Table 1 "does not include ... permanent resident, spouse or child of a Japanese national". The page does not cover an exit tax.

claims.note: Long Stay is a Designated Activities status, which sits in Table I of the Immigration Act (PwC lists the excluded statuses, and designated activities is not among them). Searched November 2026 for an FY2027 change to the foreign-national rules: none found.
claims.modelMismatch: localTaxes.ts (JP) brings overseas assets in after 10 years (afterYearsResident: 10) for everyone; for a resident on a permanent-resident or spouse status the worldwide estate is taxed from arrival. A Long Stay visitor (the profiles' case) never reaches 10 years, which the model only matches if the horizon is short.

claims.claim: A US estate and gift tax treaty exists

sources.name: IRS: Estate & gift tax treaties (international)
sources.says: All 13 countries are in the table (see us-estate-treaty-list). Estate & Gift: Australia, Austria, France, Germany, Japan, United Kingdom. Estate only: Greece, Ireland, Italy, Netherlands, South Africa, Switzerland, and Canada by Article XXIX B of the income tax treaty.

claims.note: Wording: "the US–Japan estate and gift tax treaty gives credit relief".

claims.claim: The US–Japan estate and gift tax treaty gives credit relief

sources.name: Taxes for Expats: Japan inheritance tax in 2026
sources.says: Last updated Oct 29, 2026. "the US-Japan estate tax treaty was signed in 1954 and has been in force since April 1, 1955"; "If a US citizen in Japan pays Japanese inheritance tax, they can credit that amount against their US estate tax liability."

claims.note: The treaty text was not read: the Japanese implementing act on japaneselawtranslation.go.jp is untranslated and mofa.go.jp returned HTTP 403. A dated 2026 secondary page describes the credit.

claims.claim: The $15M US estate exemption (2026) applies to a US citizen living here as anywhere

sources.name: IRS: What's new, estate and gift tax
sources.says: The table "Basic exclusion amount for year of death" has the row 2026: $15,000,000 (2025: $13,990,000). The page says the Working Families Tax Cuts, Public Law 119-21, signed July 4, 2025, "amends § 2010(c)(3) by increasing the basic exclusion amount to $15,000,000 for calendar year 2026". Page last reviewed or updated 03-Nov-2026.

sources.name: IRS: Some nonresidents with U.S. assets must file estate tax returns
sources.says: "U.S. citizens are subject to U.S. estate taxation with respect to their worldwide assets"; Form 706 is required when worldwide assets plus adjusted taxable gifts exceed the basic exclusion amount in effect on the date of death. By contrast a nonresident who is not a citizen files when US-situated assets exceed $60,000. Page last reviewed or updated 27-Jun-2026.

claims.note: Wording: "the $15M US exemption (2026) applies as anywhere".
